study_design: Population-based and hospital-based case-control study of incident prostate cancer
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Two hundred seventeen incident cases with histologically confirmed diagnosis of prostate cancer were matched to 434 hospital and community controls by age and residence.
reason: The abstract analyzes incident prostate cancer overall in a case-control study but does not define or analyze an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The prostate cancer risk increased in proportion to alpha-linolenic acid intake. In the analysis adjusting for energy and major covariables the estimated OR for upper quartile of alpha-linolenic acid was 3.1 (95% CI 1.1-3.8).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns overall incident prostate cancer, with no aggressive-disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Vitamin C intake was inversely associated with prostate cancer (OR = 0.6; 95% CI 0.3-0.9).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns prostate cancer overall rather than an aggressive incident subtype.
